report.source_text: Continuous intravenous administration of diazepam and oral addition of the antiepileptic drug topiramate (50 mg bid) were prescribed. After that, the patient recovered quickly, and follow-up EEG monitoring was normal.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old man with a history of stroke and epilepsy presented with acute visual loss, headache, and cognitive decline. Initial MRI showed marked diffuse cortical hyperintensities in the left temporoparietal and occipital lobes, and CT angiography was negative for vascular occlusion. Continuous EEG monitoring revealed continuous sharp wave discharges, especially in the left temporoparietal and occipital lobes. Treatment with continuous intravenous diazepam and oral topiramate led to quick clinical recovery and normalization of follow-up EEG, confirming Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus.
